AAPL.rationale: Apple's fundamental health is strong: Q2 FY2026 delivered a March-quarter record of $111.2B revenue (+16.6% YoY), EPS of $2.01 (+21.8% YoY), and a multi-year-high gross margin of 49% driven by record Services revenue of $31B. The balance sheet shows improving equity ($106.5B vs $66.8B a year ago) and declining debt ($82.7B vs $92.2B). Operating cash flow of $28.7B in Q2 and $53.9B in Q1 demonstrate robust cash generation. Market share gains across iPhone (21%, up from 19.5%), iPad (37%), and Apple Watch (23%) confirm competitive strength. However, the trajectory is tempered by: (1) significant QoQ declines reflecting normal seasonality but also the magnitude of the Q1 holiday quarter, (2) rising memory costs that CEO Tim Cook called a '100-year flood' threatening future margins, (3) regulatory headwinds from EU Digital Markets Act, DOJ antitrust litigation, and Italy's iCloud probe, and (4) the stock trading at 33x diluted PE — near the lower end of its 30.5-43.1 range but still a premium multiple. The P/B of 38x has compressed from 65x peak, suggesting some valuation normalization. News sentiment is mixed-to-positive (mean 0.27 over 90 days) but turned negative on June 25 (-0.176) after Apple raised MacBook/iPad prices and the stock fell 6%. The Apple-Intel chip partnership announced June 18 is a modest positive for supply chain diversification but lacks confirmed terms. No clear near-term fundamental catalyst exists to drive a re-rating; the next earnings event is likely late July/August. Overall, Apple is a high-quality franchise with solid execution but faces cost headwinds, regulatory risk, and a valuation that is fair rather than compelling.
key_factors: Record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $111.2B (+16.6% YoY) and gross margin of 49% — best March quarter ever
Services revenue at all-time high of $31B with ~76% gross margin, driving margin expansion
Market share gains: iPhone 21% (from 19.5%), iPad 37%, Apple Watch 23% per IDC/Counterpoint
Memory cost headwinds: CEO Tim Cook warned of '100-year flood' in chip costs, forcing price increases
Regulatory overhang: EU DMA, DOJ antitrust, Italy iCloud probe threaten App Store commission model
PE of 33x is mid-range vs 30.5-43.1 window; P/B compressed from 65x to 38x — not cheap but not extreme
Apple-Intel US chip partnership announced but unconfirmed — modest supply chain diversification benefit
No clear near-term re-rating catalyst before Q3 FY2026 earnings (likely late July/August)

sources_cited.excerpt: Apple CEO Tim Cook announced the company will raise prices across its product lineup due to skyrocketing memory and storage component costs. Cook described the situation as a '100-year flood'
Apple tumbled 6% after raising MacBook and iPad prices. The PCE index hit a three-year high of 4.1%
Apple secured second place, driven by the strong performance of the iPhone 17 series... 4.4% year-over-year increase in global sales for Q1
iPhone: Increased from 19% to 21%... iPad: Rose from 34% to 37%... Apple Watch: Climbed from 20% to 23%
Apple's gross margin reached 49% in Q2 FY2026, the highest level recorded across the eight-quarter income statement window. Services reached an all-time quarterly record at $31 billion
President Trump announced that Apple has agreed to work with Intel to design and build chips domestically... neither company has issued formal confirmation
